titel: The last onboarding step latches on `didFinish`, so a failed profile reload leaves the user on "Keep your profile" with a button that does nothing and an error that is never shown
Pausing the music does not pause the broadcast, and the two go-live entry points disagree about whether a paused song even counts
"Radius" means two different distances in two places, and the Discover empty state promises both in one sentence

vorschlag.text:
Alles konsistent und beide Distanzangaben beziehen sich klar auf dasselbe Discover-Radius-Konzept, nur in unterschiedlichen Rollen (Schwellenwert vs. tatsächliche Entfernung der nächsten verdeckten Person). Damit ist der Befund widerlegt.

titel: Starting a snippet leaves the primary button asserting the full song is playing on Spotify, and playState never returns to idle
"Like" (a like request sent to a person) and "Save" → "Saved to your Liked Songs" sit side by side in identical accent styling, and "Queue"/"Save" never say whose queue and library they touch

vorschlag.text:
URTEIL: nicht zutreffend
BEGRÜNDUNG: Die vier "Done"-Zustände (Like, Message, Queue-Hinweis entfällt, Save, Follow) nutzen in der gesamten App durchgängig `AppColors.live` als Bestätigungsfarbe (z. B. DiscoverCardView.swift:223/232/241, ProfileView.swift:783, OnboardingWelcomeView.swift:44) – das ist bewusstes, konsistentes Design und kein lokaler Fehler im Song-Sheet. Zudem sind "Like" und "Save" in `actionRow` (DiscoverTrackSheet.swift:434-468) nicht benachbart (Reihenfolge: Like, Message, Queue, Save, Share), tragen unterschiedliche Icons (heart-fill vs. check) und unterschiedliche Accessibility-Labels. Die behauptete Unklarheit "wessen Queue/Library" wird durch die Statusmeldungen direkt nach der Aktion aufgelöst ("Added to your queue." / "Saved to your Liked Songs.", Zeilen 648 und 678), sodass dem Nutzer unmittelbar mitgeteilt wird, dass es sein eigenes Spotify-Konto betrifft.

titel: For the person who declined, a later message is swallowed: the like is written, the message is dropped, the receiver sees nothing, and the sender is told they "already reached out"
The "N new requests" banner counts every pending request forever, so it contradicts the tab badge it is supposed to explain
In a request thread the bubble menu still offers Reply and React: Reply does nothing at all, React silently writes a reaction the sender can see while being told to keep waiting
"This is how others see you" never shows the LIVE badge or the song you're playing, which is the one thing others actually see
Music taste: "Refresh now" gives no feedback, a failed sync is silent, and the Settings footer claims data the profile does not show
Ember is no longer the one primary action per screen, and its label colour flips between near-black and white
Second vocabulary for "live", two titles for the same error alert, and the same message composer with two prompts and two different results
First-run Discover promises "you get notified", but permission was never asked in that session and nearby alerts only fire while the app is open

"You're live" is a device-local flag with no lifetime: the moment the app goes to the background the heartbeat stops and everyone else drops you from Live now, while your own screens keep claiming you are live
beleg: SocialSound-Info.plist:21-24 declares only `remote-notification` — no background processing or location mode. The two sync loops are plain `Task { while !Task.isCancelled { … sleep } }` (Services/BroadcastManager.swift:192-210, intervals at :42-43), so they are suspended with the app; NowPlayingView.swift:68-71 additionally stops the player poll on `didEnterBackground`. Viewers compute `isLive = record.isLive && now.timeIntervalSince(lastUpdate) <= maxLiveAge` with `maxLiveAge = 5 * 60` (Features/Discover/ViewModels/DiscoverViewModel.swift:523, 561) and the server flips `isLive:false` after `BROADCAST_LIVE_TTL_MINUTES = 10` (functions/src/index.ts:450, 471-476). Nothing in BroadcastManager observes scenePhase or foreground — the only `willEnterForeground` hook in the flow is NowPlayingView.swift:63-67, and it touches the view model, not the broadcast. The same assumption breaks the idle watchdog: `maxIdlePolls = 40 // ≈ 10 minutes at 15s` (BroadcastManager.swift:49) can only elapse while the user sits in the foreground app with nothing playing.

titel: When the Spotify grant dies while live, the broadcast neither ends nor is mentioned: the heartbeat keeps re-asserting isLive with a frozen track, the idle watchdog can no longer fire, and one UI branch has no way to stop
beleg: On a rejected refresh token, SpotifyAuthManager.swift:163-168 calls `disconnect()` and sets `loginExpired = true` — but never touches BroadcastManager. (The intent is clear elsewhere: the manual Settings disconnect explicitly stops the broadcast first, SettingsContentView.swift:306-319 "This ends your live session.") `loginExpired` is read only in Features/Discover/Views/DiscoverTrackSheet.swift:590, 682 — not on the Live tab, not on the go-live banner, not in BroadcastManager. The idle watchdog cannot help: `if let state = try? await SpotifyService.shared.fetchNowPlayingState()` wraps the whole counter, so a throwing poll never increments `idlePolls` (BroadcastManager.swift:244-257). Worse, `syncTrack` runs regardless and `upsertBroadcast` always writes `"isLive": true` plus a fresh `updatedAt` (BroadcastManager.swift:259, 274-288, 334-368), so the server's staleness sweep (functions/src/index.ts:471-476) can never expire it either. And NowPlayingView.swift:92-93 routes to `spotifyDisconnectedState` (:292-337), which contains no live badge and no `CompactBroadcastToggle` — reachable while broadcasting whenever `vm.currentTrack` is nil (set to nil on `noActiveDevice`, NowPlayingViewModel.swift:73-81).
